REGISTRY_CLAIM='held' and a test asserts it is NOT 'measured': a measured label over this set would be a value carrying a FALSE claim, strictly worse than the list itself, because a fake predicate invites a successor to 'fix' a predicate that was never the mechanism. REGISTRY_VERSION='1.0'. THE MAINTAINER SLOT IS None BY DESIGN and MAINTAINER_STATUS carries the words 'not a build gate' -- the test ASSERTS THE STATE and does NOT enforce a gate, which is the distinction that keeps this from becoming the manufactured friction CLAUDE.md forbids. Membership verified against the roster at the declared vintage: for all nine members the declared model_id and account_count match the artifact row exactly (15/3, 30/4, 40/18, 50/83, 60/81, 70/39, 80/65, 90/0, 98/11). The roster's own envelope carries the coverage: pageCount=1, totalResultCount=65, len(pagedResults)=65 -- FULL COVERAGE read from the artifact, not inferred. THE WHY IS ON THE FACE TOO: both candidate planes are recorded as measured-with-controls, so a successor cannot mistake the list for a failure of effort -- the roster's only evaluable discriminators are accountCount (disowned by Andrew) and displayName (disowned by SAT-b-2), while id/lastUpdate/name/rowNumber are ROW-UNIQUE and therefore VACUOUSLY disjoint between any two disjoint row sets, which is identity and not class information.

acceptance.criterion_verbatim: Opal Ultra Short Term is ABSENT from the member set, and the artifact records that it IS a real model (6 accounts) -- roster membership is not satellite membership
acceptance.output_evidence: ABSENT FROM THE MEMBERS, PRESENT ON THE ROSTER, AND THE RECORD SAYS WHY. 'Opal Ultra Short Term' is not in MEMBER_NAMES. It IS carried in NOT_A_SATELLITE_BUT_A_REAL_MODEL with account_count=6, model_type='Strategy', model_id 42642a1a-a0a8-4171-9c89-c3c5e2939533, and Andrew's ruling quoted VERBATIM ('that was erroneously included in a screenshot because an Opal employee sloppily screenshotted a spreadsheet, not because it is a member of the Satellites group'). THE EXISTENCE HALF IS EXERCISED AGAINST THE ARTIFACT, NOT ASSERTED: the test finds the row on the 2026-08-27 roster and asserts accountCount==6 and id==the recorded id -- so this is an EXCLUSION OF A REAL BOOK rather than a name that failed to match. Were it merely absent from the feed, that assertion would FAIL and the record would be describing something that does not exist. The drift oracle does NOT surface it (it is not canonical-form), so the exclusion costs no recurring question.

acceptance.criterion_verbatim: Exercised on the 98 pair specifically: Core | Satellite 98 (9) and Opal Satellite 98 (11) are SEPARATED. Also show a predicate written against 'Core | Satellite' misses Core / Satellite Equity (a SLASH) -- declare the frame if you state any excluded-row count
acceptance.output_evidence: SEPARATED, AND THE MUTANT PREDICATES WERE RUN RATHER THAN DESCRIBED -- WHICH FOUND A THIRD ROW THE TO DID NOT NAME. Measured: Core | Satellite 98 accountCount=9, Opal Satellite 98 accountCount=11; only the latter is in MEMBER_NAMES and only the latter is returned by canonical_roster_names. THE TRAILING-NUMBER PREDICATE IS WORSE THAN THE TO STATED: rows ending '98' are {Core | Satellite 98, Opal Satellite 98, PASSIVE 98} -- a book from an unrelated family entirely. The TO named the Core-family collision; the roster carries a THIRD row, measured rather than predicted. The unanchored 'Satellite 98' form is narrower but still admits the wrong book. ONLY THE ANCHORED CANONICAL FORM SEPARATES ALL THREE, and that is asserted as a set intersection rather than left as prose. THE SLASH TRAP, EXERCISED: names starting 'Core | Satellite' number 15 and MISS 'Core / Satellite Equity'; 15 + 1 = 16 accounts for every 'Core '-prefixed row, asserted so neither separator can be dropped silently. The registry is NOT exposed to this, because membership is anchored POSITIVELY on the canonical Opal form rather than by blacklisting family spellings -- a blacklist must enumerate every separator someone might type and silently admits the one it forgot. EVERY COUNT NAMES ITS FRAME AND IS RE-MEASURED IN THE TEST (SAT-b-4's withdrawn '19' is not restated in any form): canonical ^Opal Satellite <N>$ = 9; contains 'satellite' case-insensitively and not canonical = 18; matches /sat/i and not canonical = 21; starts with 'Core ' = 16. All four over the declared denominator of 65 rows at 2026-08-27.

acceptance.criterion_verbatim: The drift detector rides SAT-b-2's EXISTING oracle (NO new monitor/alarm/checker -- the moratorium binds): canonical Opal Satellite <N> roster rows printed beside the declared nine, FAIL on symmetric difference IN EITHER DIRECTION. Exercise the ADD direction -- an undercount announces itself, an overcount never does
acceptance.output_evidence: BOTH DIRECTIONS MADE TO FAIL ON DEMAND, WITH THE CLEAN CASE AS THE POSITIVE CONTROL. NO NEW MONITOR: drift_report/assert_no_drift are functions a test calls at BUILD time -- nothing schedules, nothing alarms, nothing sends. The moratorium is respected by construction and the module says so on its face. CLEAN CASE: at the declared vintage the declared nine and the roster's canonical rows are IDENTICAL, both printed beside each other with the roster-row denominator (65). ADD DIRECTION (the one that matters, and the one almost never tested): injecting a synthetic 'Opal Satellite 55' row yields ok=False, on_roster_not_declared=['Opal Satellite 55'], declared_not_on_roster=[], and assert_no_drift RAISES SatelliteRegistryDrift naming the row. That is the case where an UNDERCOUNT announces itself but an OVERCOUNT never does -- a newly minted satellite is simply, silently, not on the page. REMOVE DIRECTION: dropping Opal Satellite 90 from the roster yields declared_not_on_roster=['Opal Satellite 90'] and raises. The raise message directs a human to edit SATELLITE_MEMBERS deliberately and EXPLICITLY FORBIDS widening CANONICAL_NAME_FORM to make it pass, which would turn the drift detector back into the membership heuristic Andrew disowned. THE WRONG KEY IS PROVEN WRONG RATHER THAN MERELY AVOIDED: keying the oracle on displayName instead of name yields EIGHT canonical rows, not nine -- it drops Opal Satellite 60 ('Opal - Satellite 60' does not match the canonical form) and would report the 81-account book as MISSING on EVERY build, while reading None for the 40 rows carrying no displayName. The set difference is asserted to be exactly {Opal Satellite 60}, which is where AC3's dash hazard and AC4's oracle meet.
acceptance.denominator: 9 declared vs 9 observed at vintage over 65 rows; 2 drift directions each exercised and each raising; 1 wrong-key control yielding 8 of 9

acceptance.criterion_verbatim: Whether Opal Satellite 90 (0 accounts) renders is DECIDED AND STATED on the artifact, not resolved by accident of the predicate
acceptance.output_evidence: DECIDED: RENDER. STATED AS ITS OWN CONSTANT, WITH ITS OWN CLAIM, SEPARABLE FROM MEMBERSHIP. RENDER_ZERO_ACCOUNT_MEMBERS=True and RENDER_ZERO_ACCOUNT_MEMBERS_CLAIM='held'. It is a SEPARATE constant from the member set on purpose -- Rule 24(iii): membership and display are two axes, and folding them into one enum is exactly how a 0-account book gets decided by accident. TWO CITABLE REASONS, NOT AESTHETIC ONES: (1) Positioning renders a book's COMPOSITION, not its assets, and account count never enters the arithmetic -- VERIFIED IN THE TEST, Satellite 90 resolves to a COMPLETE composition (ULT 1.0), identical in book and weight to the 11-account Satellite 98, so hiding it would suppress a correct panel for an unrelated reason; (2) THE PLANE ALREADY RULED THIS SHAPE -- bookSet.ts resolveBooks states 'DECLARED ORDER IS THE FLOOR ... every declared book always renders (so a book missing from the payload still shows its column with N/A)', so hiding a declared member on an account threshold would CONTRADICT the sibling mode on the same page. Measured at the vintage: accountCount=0 and it IS in MEMBER_NAMES -- IN by declaration despite zero accounts, which is the OPPOSITE of a threshold. THE DECISION IS RATIFIABLE: it carries claim 'held' and is written down precisely so the registry maintainer can OVERTURN it deliberately at ship rather than discover it.
acceptance.denominator: 1 of 9 members carries accountCount=0; its composition compared against 1 non-zero-account member and found identical in book and weight
